verdict.rationale: Greptile explicitly markets 'complete understanding of your codebase' and one HN user confirms it surfaced cross-file, historically accurate context (BigDecimal encoding) that saved real time (greptile-comm-1), while another employer report says it 'catches real issues' (greptile-comm-8). However a hands-on report on a C++ codebase found Greptile 'really bad at analyzing templates' with answers 'always incomplete and usually partly or mostly incorrect, even when comments in source code answer the question' (greptile-comm-3), directly contradicting the whole-repo-understanding claim for non-trivial cases. Missing for 10: systematic evidence (benchmarks, more hands-on reports) on whether review comments consistently reference call sites/conventions across languages, and resolution of the template-analysis failure.
